name: bonk-sir-g4-the-bonk
notes: Sir Bonk ground.4 (anim.bonk.g4), 2026-10-22: The BONK, the owner's heavy kill strike from the normals board (tmp/bonk-normals) and the Seedance 2.5 reference the owner approved (artifacts/video-refs/sir-bonk-normals/g4-the-bonk). Two-handed overhead smash, no gags (normals stay simple; the video's trembling tell becomes a slow loaded hold). Today's move-data clock (118 ticks, plank hitbox 48-63, IASA 71). Replaces Heavy Double Slice. Lessons from Barn Door and Sunrise built in: loose two-handed hold with elbows under the hands (elbows='hands' overhead), carry both ways, flow in the first take, body mechanics (stance, hip and chest drive, a real stamp), arc targets from hitarc.py, save early.
character: Sir Bonk (68 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names and full fingers; a 3x4 cape chain Cape_L/C/R1..4 under Spine2 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest; a 2.26 m wooden plank greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0, bladeHilt where its 1.42 m blade leaves the crossguard and bladeEnd at the tip)
description:
Sir Bonk's ground 4, The BONK: his kill strike. He hauls the plank up and far back over his head with both hands, leaning back with his left knee lifted high on one leg, holds that loaded pose for a long readable beat, then stamps forward and brings the plank down over the top onto the floor in front of him with his whole body weight, knees bending deep into the impact, and heaves it back onto his right shoulder. Very heavy. It replaces his old Heavy Double Slice.

Who he is. Sir Bonk is a huge, good-hearted, slightly dumb brute who read Don Quixote once and knighted himself (images 1 and 2). He has a blue mop-bucket helm with a broom crest, a cream tabard with his painted crown, pot-lid pauldrons and a cape, and he carries a plank greatsword. The owner wants his normals clean: no gags, the energy comes from his body.

His idle, where this move starts and ends (character frame, metres from the entry hips): feet wide and square to the front (foot joints about -0.89 up, the floor at -1.025). The plank rests back over his right shoulder: the right hand in front of the right chest (about 0.46 m above the hips), the blade rising behind him to his right, its tip about 1.15 m behind his hips and 0.9 m above the hilt. The left fist sits on his left hip. Shoulders about 0.53 m above the hips, head joint 0.66 m, each arm about 0.70 m from shoulder to wrist.

How the game plays it. Ticks 0-118 at 60 Hz, played once; the game stretches the clip over the move, so author exactly these ticks. The plank itself is the hitbox (a 0.5 m capsule along it) from tick 48 to tick 63: it must be coming down over the top at tick 48 and on the floor in front of him by about tick 52, staying low and ahead until tick 63. Tick 0 is the idle pose exactly; from tick 71 the player can act again, so the plank is back on his shoulder by 71, and ticks 80-118 are the idle pose exactly. Contact is tick 48; nothing before it hits, so the wind-up of ticks 0-47 is the tell.

The arc is the move. The plank is the hitbox, so its path in ticks 48-63 decides who it hits (owner: for weapon normals the arc is the most important part). It comes over the top and down: at tick 46 straight up above his head, at tick 48 about 45 degrees forward and down (in front of his face), at tick 50-52 sweeping to flat on the floor ahead of him, tip 2.2-2.6 m in front of his hips and a hand's width off the floor, hilt about 1 m ahead and 0.5 m up, and it stays there pressed into the floor to tick 63 as he sinks into the lunge. A sketch of that path touches about 108 FightGuy and Manki positions, standing ones from 0.25 to 3.0 m ahead (`hitarc.py`). The brief's `arc` targets count them.

The reference (image 3: eleven frames of the video the owner approved, front three-quarter right; each frame's tick is in the brief's review beats). It sets poses and body mechanics, not timing: the video holds every pose far longer.

The beats:
- Ticks 0-3: he leaves the idle. Its plank hand is folded back about 137 degrees off the forearm; straighten that wrist by tick 4 (the check skips ticks 0-3).
- Ticks 3-6, grip (video beat 2): the left hand leaves his hip and closes on the handle just under the right hand; the plank comes upright in front of his right shoulder.
- Ticks 6-14, lift (beat 3): both hands haul the plank up over the head and back behind him, the chest and head leaning back, the right leg taking his weight, the left knee starting to rise.
- Ticks 14-42, the tell (beat 4-5): loaded on one leg: the left knee high (thigh about horizontal), the plank cocked behind his head pointing down and back, both hands above and behind his head, the chest arched back, his weight on the right leg. This is a moving hold, never frozen: the knee creeps higher, the chest leans further back, the hands sink a little, a held-breath tension building to tick 42. The left foot must not touch the floor.
- Ticks 42-46, commit (beat 6-7): the left leg stamps forward and down, the hips drop and drive forward first, the chest folds forward after them, the plank whips up and over the top: straight up above his head at tick 46 (beat 7), both hands overhead.
- Ticks 46-48: the left foot plants well ahead (0.4-0.5 m) at about tick 47; the plank is 45 degrees down in front of his face at tick 48 (contact), the body falling into the stamp, both knees bent.
- Ticks 48-53, slam (beat 8-9): the chest folds over and the arms follow the plank down; it lands flat on the floor ahead, his weight deep in a lunge: the left knee bent far over the planted left foot, the hips 20-30 cm below the idle, the right leg trailing straight, the right heel up.
- Ticks 53-63, impact held: the plank stays pressed on the floor ahead while he sinks a little further and the cape catches up: a moving hold, not frozen.
- Ticks 63-71, heave (beat 10-11): the hands lift the plank and the body unfolds; the plank is vertical in front of him at about tick 66 (beat 10); the left hand lets go (by tick 66) and heads for his hip; the plank settles onto his right shoulder where the idle carries it at tick 71, the left foot stepping back toward its idle place.
- Ticks 71-80: straight into his idle pose, no separate settle. The plank wrist folds back to the idle's 137 degrees as the plank lands (the check skips ticks 64-118 for it). Ticks 80-118 hold the idle pose exactly.

Both hands, loosely. Both hands hold the handle from tick 6 to tick 66 (the brief's `two_hands`, held loosely: `two_hands_hold`). The left fist only has to sit on the handle beside the right hand, free to turn about it and slide along it: `two_hand_grip(..., hold='loose', elbows=...)` with elbows='hands' for the keys with the hands at or above the head (lift, tell, over, commit) and elbows=True for the others; between the keys `carry(clip, keys, hold='loose', elbows=..., both_ways=True)` per stretch. From tick 66 the right hand carries the plank alone. Elbows never wing up and out sideways.

The body drives the strike. The load is his whole back arching and the knee drawn up; the release is the hips driving forward and down, then the chest folding, then the arms: the arms only follow. Stagger the arrivals (hips first, the chest a tick or two later, the arms and head trailing; a body part may meet its key up to 2 ticks early or late, the plank keeps its key ticks). The plank's direction turns smoothly about the hands with no flips; the left forearm twists spread over several ticks, with the loose hold turning about the handle.

Flow: follow the guide's Flow section: moving holds, the spine flexing against the hips, the head lagging. Before saving, check the `flow:` metrics: under 1.0 stops per joint per second and under 30% of the body stopping together. Save a clip within 15 minutes of starting the motion.

Feet: the right foot is planted from tick 5 to about tick 66 (a heel may lift in the lunge, the ball stays put). The left foot leaves the floor at about tick 10, is high from tick 14 to 42, stamps at about tick 47 and then stays planted to tick 66. Both end in their idle places by tick 80. The plank stays clear of his bucket, crest, pauldrons, cape and legs, and its tip never goes into the floor (floor at up = -1.025 m in the character frame). The fighter does not move; the hips may travel with the stamp. Do not animate the cape joints (Cape_L/C/R1..4). No props other than the plank. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees) outside the exempt ticks.
